walkthroughs.body_html:
Computers — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Computers brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Computers.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which technique involves breaking a problem into smaller sub-problems?
options: Abstraction
Decomposition
Iteration
Encapsulation

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of a trace table?
options: To compile code
To track variable values during execution
To draw a flowchart
To store program output

mcqs.q: What is the denary value of binary 10110?
options: 10110 (treating it as a denary number).
To make the function run faster.
11 (counting the 1s).

mcqs.q: Why must a recursive function have a base case?
options: Because UDP is always faster than TCP.
Without it, the function calls itself indefinitely, causing a stack overflow.
Because the syntax requires it.
To make the function run faster.

mcqs.q: Why is UDP used for live video streaming despite being unreliable?
options: Because UDP is always faster than TCP.
Because TCP cannot handle video data.
Lower overhead and latency - retransmitting late packets would harm real-time quality.
To make the function run faster.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Decomposition”?
options: Structured English-like description of an algorithm, independent of any programming language.
Removing unnecessary detail from a problem to focus on the essential features.
Breaking a complex problem into smaller, more manageable sub-problems.
A finite, ordered sequence of unambiguous steps that solves a problem or completes a task.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Abstraction”?
options: A finite, ordered sequence of unambiguous steps that solves a problem or completes a task.
Table used to track the changing values of variables as an algorithm executes step by step.
Structured English-like description of an algorithm, independent of any programming language.
Removing unnecessary detail from a problem to focus on the essential features.
